images.text:
Miranda: Welcome back to the office! I wanted to take a moment to congratulate you all on everything you've done. All your hard work is greatly appreciated.
Peter: It wouldn't have been possible without you, Miranda.
Miranda: You're so sweet, Peter! How did everyone enjoy the party?
Renata: It was a blast! You did great on the catwalk, Miranda - you looked very fashionable. I loved that soft pink chiffon suit with rhinestones.
Rocco: Holly's has made drastic improvements with this clothing line. Everything looks really trendy. I didn't see a single frumpy outfit except for that suede wrap dress. What an ugly piece!
Miranda: Really? I thought the denim jumpsuit looked marvelous!

Miranda: What did you think of Farmani's speech? What an amazing speech, right?
Peter: Yeah, he was quite convincing and he looked radiant. He really prepared for that moment!
Renata: I agree, but that suit he wore. That was quite the showstopper.

Miranda: Mmm, the pinstripes were a nice touch. Anyway, thank you everyone for your tremendous work - it was a superb event! With everyone's help we managed to pull things off in a short time. Peter, you were a great porter! Your quick thinking on practical details saved the day ... and you kept Ricardo Verde in a good mood. You handled that job very well.
Peter: Thanks, Miranda. Ricardo ended up being a fantastic MC.
Janet: Miranda, would you come to my office please? An urgent matter suddenly came up.

You use the Simple Past tense to talk about different kinds of past events: short, quickly finished actions, longer situations and repeated events.
Usually, when you use the Simple Past tense, the time of the finished action is clear from the context or explicitly mentioned in the sentence.

For example:
I thought the denim jumpsuit looked marvelous!
Here, it is clear when the action of “thinking” happened and that it finished.

Here is another example:
How did everyone enjoy the party last night?
Remember that there are both regular and irregular verbs. Look at the chart for examples of the Simple Past tense verbs.
I loved that soft pink chiffon suit with rhinestones.
I thought the denim jumpsuit looked marvelous!
I didn't see a single frumpy outfit except for that suede wrap dress.
What did you think of Farmani's speech?
Yeah, he was quite convincing and he looked radiant.
You give a compliment or praise to ease communication.
Compliments and praise are used socially to develop a relationship between two people.

You can use them to start a conversation with someone you don't know well or have just met. They are used in a work environment to encourage employees and strengthen morale. You can compliment or praise someone's work.

You can compliment someone on the work they did by using phrases like:
  • ... to congratulate you (all) on ..
  • It wouldn't have been ...
  • All your ...
  • You + verb ...
  • That is/was ...
  • What a ...!
  • Thank you ...

You can use adjectives like:
  • sweet
  • great
  • fantastic
  • tremendous
  • amazing
  • superb
I wanted to congratulate you on a job well done!
I loved that soft pink chiffon suit with rhinestones.
You handled that job very well.
